items.title: Billy Taylor — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Duke Pierson coming along with the big band. I mean a lot of stuff should have happened with that big band.

ctx.x: Walter Davis I mean, thank you. Walter Davis and who else? There was another pianist that they recorded as… Harsh Pollen, you know. These were guys who with merchandizing, given the strength of the label at that time could have gone much further and could have done much more then they were able to do. But Bluenote just put the records out. Symphony Sid and the other good jazz disc jockeys around the country played them because they were Bluenote records and they were good. Duke Pierson coming along

with the big band. I mean a lot of stuff should have happened with that big band. It was a great big band. Many things that they could have done in terms of promotion and merchandizing were not done because that wasn’t the way they did business at the Prestege or the Bluenote or the Roost or any of those labels. So that wasn’t… you put the record out if it gets to a disc jockey or gets on a juke box you might put a single out from the record if it looks like it is getting a lot of play or can get a lot of play.…
